Job Context:  The Team Leader will lead project delivery by connecting district-level responses with national legal, advocacy and management support. The position will establish clear responsibilities between the different clusters and departments of Head Office, unit offices, Legal Team and collaborating organisations; coordinate prompt action following reported violence; and ensure sustained follow-up with affected individuals and families. The Team Leader will develop and implement an advocacy and partnership strategy with like-minded organisations, using documented cases to seek specific protection measures, legal remedies, access to services and institutional improvements. The role will also ensure reliable incident records, coordinated case reviews, functioning district platforms, accountable use of project funds and timely reporting. The Team Leader is responsible for organising, assigning, tracking, and escalating actions. Submit a monthly consolidated update to the Project Management Team (including Director Programme, Director Legal, Director Advocacy and Communication), identifying progress, unresolved barriers and decisions required from senior management, i.e., Honorary Executive Director. Arrange direct coordination between district staff and the relevant legal, protection, advocacy or finance personnel when a matter requires specialist input. Maintain one project action tracker with the help of the MEAL team, assigning each action to a named person with a deadline and completion evidence. Establish a contact and escalation list identifying the primary and alternate focal persons in each unit office and the relevant Head Office teams. Establish a written incident-response procedure during the first month, and arrange an initial assessment with the relevant Unit Coordinator or alternate focal person. Record the source, location, reported harm, immediate risks, and assistance already available. For reports indicating immediate danger, initiate coordination on the same day the information is received. Notify the programme supervisor and relevant Legal Team focal person of serious incidents, identifying decisions or resources required. Case Coordination and Continuing Support: Agree case priorities with the Legal Team and Unit Coordinators, considering protection risks, detention, upcoming hearings, investigation delays and the wishes of affected individuals. Ensure each supported case records the assigned lawyer, unit focal person, current procedural stage, next hearing or deadline, and required action. Convene monthly case strategy reviews with relevant lawyers and unit staff, with additional reviews for urgent cases. Discussions will focus on existing barriers and practical next steps. Track implementation of agreed legal and administrative actions. Refer questions about legal arguments, remedies,s or representation to the assigned lawyers. Ensure unit staff communicate material developments to clients and families and record outstanding questions or concerns. Separate urgent case-related advocacy from longer-term institutional advocacy. Urgent engagement should seek a defined response, such as protection, action on a complaint, or access to assistance. Use recurring findings from cases and fact-finding reports to prepare submissions and briefings for relevant institutions, including the National Human Rights Commission, Directorate of Bangladesh Legal Aid and appropriate government authorities. Coordinate national meetings around specific requests and documented cases. Record commitments and assign responsibility for follow-up. Work with district staff to communicate agreed requests to local administration, police, District Legal Aid Committees and service providers. Obtain approval before issuing public statements or sharing sensitive case information. Partnerships with like-minded Organisations: Map organisations working on minority rights, legal aid, documentation, protection and survivor support, identifying their district presence and practical contribution. Agree collaboration arrangements for selected activities, such as joint fact-finding, protection referrals, legal support, evidence review and advocacy. Record focal persons, tasks, information-sharing conditions and approval requirements. Maintain an agreed contact mechanism for rapid coordination following serious incidents. Convene quarterly national coordination meetings to review shared concerns, identify joint action and assess progress on previous commitments. District Platforms and Referral Networks: Ensure each Solidarity and Security Platform maintains an updated membership list, contact directory, meeting schedule and record of agreed actions.
